description: Provenance for the draft FHGM conformance suite. The suite is model-level: it validates FHGM records embedded in FHGFF3 1.1 files against the reviewed native draft contract, so it depends on one released external artifact (the base schema) and on the contract and generator bytes carried in this repository. scripts/check_header_parity.py applies the same discipline to the pinned header/ tree; run_conformance.py verifies every digest below on each run and refuses to report a pass when a recorded artifact changed under the manifest. Nothing here is a schema authority: FHGM has no released contract, no schemaVersion, no schema URL and no versions.json row, and selection rule V7 keeps it that way until the shared publication PR lands.

baseSchema.commitNote: The commit the v0.5.0 tag names. It is not an ancestor of shared main: the v0.5.0 release was tagged before its merge commit landed, a split recorded in the workspace guide and not repeated for later releases.
baseSchema.crossCheck: validate_fhgm.py pins the same digest as BASE_SHA256 and refuses any other bytes; run_conformance.py compares this record, those bytes and the checker's constant and reports all three. The released file is also what development/examples/contract, development/examples/model and development/examples/s6k were validated against in PRs #7, #10 and #11.
baseSchema.whyThisRelease: The draft transport pins the released FHGFF3 1.1 identity (fhgm-draft.schema.schema.json enum), and 1.1 was published at v0.5.0. FHGFF3 1.2 arrived at v0.6.0 and changes no FHGM rule; moving the transport floor is a separate contract decision, not a side effect of this suite.

contractArtifacts.note: Reviewed in place on 2026-11-14: the 2026-11-12 proposal bytes (commit 8b0ca00, sha256 9114780bfcc8b575fa660b2d38a7ad521d9b993d2544963cdad388daed045e27) carry the same title, field names, requiredness and keywords; only description text changed to record the review's positions, so no validation outcome moved and the draft label stays v0.1.

contractArtifacts.role: model-level checker (K3-K6), the authority for every recorded outcome

vectorGenerators.role: generates the v0.1 fixture set that this suite cites in place (PR #11 bytes, unchanged)
derives the S6k record vector from the committed profile fixture
shared render, canonical-JSON and checksum helpers reused by both generators (PR #4 pilot machinery)

emits the promoted real-data vectors named dmel-* from the committed examples/dmel4 fixtures (draft promotion packet, PROMOTION-2026-11-15.md; one documented header mutation per case, canonical render with a fresh checksum, feature bytes untouched)

observedWith.note: Every recorded outcome comes from a run of development/model/validate_fhgm.py with these versions. check_draft.py was additionally re-run with fair-bioheaders 0.8.1 (the shared conformance job's toolkit baseline in this repository's header-parity.yml), and run_conformance.py passed end to end under 0.8.1 as well, so no outcome here depends on a toolkit newer than the one that job installs. The GFF3 feature lane was observed twice: with gff3-validator 0.1.0 built from the local gff3-validator checkout and with the 0.1.0 wheel installed from PyPI (the CI environment); both report zero errors and zero warnings on every vector of the census at recording time: the 31 pre-promotion vectors (2026-11-14) and, in a re-run on 2026-11-15 with the 12 promoted dmel-* entries present, all 43. The 2026-11-15 real-data promotion batch (12 dmel-* vectors, draft packet PROMOTION-2026-11-15.md) was observed the same way with these versions; the wrong-parent digest inside dmel-reference-contradicts-file is the committed S6k fixture's own checksum, read from its bytes at generation time, not transcribed.

independence.checksum: run_conformance.py recomputes each vector's file-bound SHA-512/256 with hashlib over the exact bytes minus the root checksum line, as a second implementation next to the toolkit's, and requires the two to agree with the value the header states before it reports the model layer.
independence.vectorOutcomes: No expectation in manifest.json was written from reading the code. Each one was observed by running the committed checker over the generated bytes, and run_conformance.py re-observes it on every run.
independence.notRun: gff3-validate 0.1.0 (local checkout build and the PyPI wheel) ran the feature layer over every vector; the lane is optional at run time and reports skipped where the tool is absent. Header checks were deliberately skipped with --no-header, because the FHGFF3 header identity is the base layer of this suite, not its subject.

syntheticContent.statement: Every vector except s6k-derived-record-fixture is synthetic. The accession SYNTHETIC_ASSEMBLY.1 and the SeqCol digest come from the revision pilot's one-record toy collection (>toy with 100 'A' bases), the accessions, model IDs, DOIs, URNs and evidence strings are placeholders scoped to these directories, and the synthetic FHR parent digest is computed over declared synthetic bytes. No accession, digest, identifier or biological relationship was invented for a real resource. The dmel-* promotion-batch vectors are NOT synthetic: their feature rows, accessions, coordinates, identifiers and pointers come verbatim or by documented single-field mutation from the real-data fixtures under development/examples/dmel4/ (RefSeq GCF_000001215.4, chromosome NC_004353.4; see that directory's SOURCE.md and provenance.json); the only invented token is the clearly labelled gene-Dmel_absentFromThisFile, which asserts absence from the file and names no real resource.
syntheticContent.attribution: s6k-derived-record-fixture wraps a feature payload derived from Laura K. Reed, 'Model: Gene model for the ortholog of S6k in Drosophila ananassae', CaltechDATA v1.0, CC BY 4.0 (deposit https://doi.org/10.22002/e86gh-a7p16), as recorded in development/examples/s6k/README.md. Its record reuses only identifiers, attribution and the verified reference result already recorded there.
